primary_outputs: Sample mean, standard deviation (SD), sample size and measurement units.
inference_and_tests: Descriptive only; no intrinsic hypothesis test. If generalizing to a population, report the sampling design and an appropriate confidence interval for its mean.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Mean and SD are in the original units; the standard error and a confidence interval describe precision of the mean, not dispersion of individual values.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check coverage, missingness, outliers and distribution; model fit indices are not applicable.
interpretation_guidance: A mean of 125 mmHg describes the sample average; SD of 15 mmHg describes variation among observations.
common_misinterpretations: Do not call mean ± SD a confidence interval or interpret a small SD as high precision of the population mean.
reporting_example: Among [n] participants, mean [measure] was [mean] [units] (SD [SD]); [missing] values were missing.

primary_outputs: Median, 25th and 75th percentiles (Q1 and Q3), interquartile range (IQR) and sample size.
inference_and_tests: Descriptive only; a separate inferential procedure is required for a hypothesis test or confidence interval for the population median.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: IQR = Q3 − Q1 describes the middle 50% of measurements; confidence intervals for the median need a separate procedure.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Review skew, outliers, missing values and ties; conventional model fit statistics do not apply.
interpretation_guidance: A median of $50 describes the midpoint; Q1–Q3 of $30–$90 describes the spread of the central half.
common_misinterpretations: An IQR is neither the full observed range nor a confidence interval around the median.
reporting_example: Median [measure] was [median] (Q1–Q3: [Q1]–[Q3]; n = [n]).

primary_outputs: Category counts, denominators, proportions or percentages, optionally by subgroup.
inference_and_tests: Descriptive only; binomial or multinomial uncertainty may be estimated where sampling assumptions permit.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Percentage and its denominator should be reported together; an appropriate confidence interval describes population-proportion uncertainty.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check missing categories, small cells and weighting; no model fit measure is inherent.
interpretation_guidance: Twenty of 80 participants (25%) fall into the specified category.
common_misinterpretations: Do not compare percentages without checking denominators or equate raw sample counts with representative population estimates.
reporting_example: [count]/[denominator] participants ([percent]%) had [category]; [missing] records were missing.

primary_outputs: Pearson correlation r, sample size and optionally a scatterplot.
inference_and_tests: Test of zero population linear correlation typically uses a t statistic and p-value; confidence intervals often use Fisher z under suitable assumptions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: r ranges from −1 to +1; report a confidence interval for the correlation and consider r² only as the shared linear variation in a simple bivariate setting.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect scatterplot for linearity and influential observations; correlation is not assessed by regression fit metrics alone.
interpretation_guidance: Positive r indicates that larger X tends to accompany larger Y in an approximately linear pattern.
common_misinterpretations: A large correlation does not establish causality, and r near zero does not rule out a nonlinear association.
reporting_example: X and Y had Pearson r = [r] (95% CI [lower], [upper]; n = [n]; p = [p]).

primary_outputs: Spearman rank correlation ρ (rho), sample size and rank scatterplot.
inference_and_tests: A test of no monotonic association yields a p-value; exact or approximate methods depend on sample size and ties.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: ρ ranges from −1 to +1; report an appropriate uncertainty interval if inferential interpretation is intended.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect monotonicity, ties, and influential rankings; conventional model fit indices do not apply.
interpretation_guidance: Positive ρ suggests observations with higher X tend to rank higher on Y.
common_misinterpretations: It does not measure linear change per unit, prove causation, or reliably capture a U-shaped relationship.
reporting_example: Spearman ρ = [rho] (n = [n], p = [p]); ties were [handled/how].

primary_outputs: Two independent-group means, pooled-variance t statistic and degrees of freedom.
inference_and_tests: Two-sided or prespecified one-sided t test provides a p-value for equal population means under the model.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Mean difference with a confidence interval; optionally Cohen d with clear pooled-SD definition.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Review group independence, variance homogeneity and relevant residual behavior; no global model fit index is required.
interpretation_guidance: The signed mean difference quantifies how much higher the outcome is in one group.
common_misinterpretations: A non-significant p-value is not evidence of equivalence; unequal variances can invalidate pooled-variance inference.
reporting_example: Mean difference (group A − B) = [diff] [units] (95% CI [lower], [upper]); t([df]) = [t], p = [p].

primary_outputs: Two means, Welch t statistic and Satterthwaite-adjusted degrees of freedom.
inference_and_tests: Welch test provides a p-value for a group-mean difference without assuming equal group variances.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Unpooled mean difference and confidence interval are central; standardized differences require a declared denominator.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect independent sampling, outliers and distribution; no conventional model-fit statistic.
interpretation_guidance: The group difference is interpreted in outcome units, with inference robust to unequal variances under appropriate sampling.
common_misinterpretations: Welch does not fix dependence, severe distribution problems in very small samples, or confounding.
reporting_example: Welch mean difference = [diff] [units] (95% CI [lower], [upper]); t([df]) = [t], p = [p].

primary_outputs: Mean within-person difference, SD of paired differences, t statistic and degrees of freedom.
inference_and_tests: Paired t test evaluates whether the mean paired difference is zero.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report paired mean difference with confidence interval; optionally standardized paired effect size with its definition.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check matched identity and distribution of differences; no model fit index.
interpretation_guidance: A negative post-minus-pre difference indicates an average decrease after the later measurement.
common_misinterpretations: Do not treat the two observations as independent or interpret a before–after change as causal without design support.
reporting_example: Mean paired (post − pre) change = [diff] [units] (95% CI [lower], [upper]); t([df]) = [t], p = [p].

primary_outputs: Mann–Whitney U (or Wilcoxon rank-sum W) statistic, sample sizes and rank distributions.
inference_and_tests: Rank-based test assesses distributional differences; a location-shift interpretation requires additional shape assumptions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report probability of superiority or rank-biserial effect with interval when possible; Hodges–Lehmann shift may be used under a location-shift model.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect group distributions, shapes and ties; no model fit index.
interpretation_guidance: A high probability-of-superiority estimate means a randomly sampled value from one group is often larger than one from the other.
common_misinterpretations: The U test is not universally a test of medians and does not automatically adjust for confounders.
reporting_example: Mann–Whitney U = [U] (n1 = [n1], n2 = [n2], p = [p]); rank-based effect = [effect].

primary_outputs: Wilcoxon signed-rank statistic, paired-difference ranks and number of nonzero pairs.
inference_and_tests: Tests symmetry-centered paired differences around zero under its standard location interpretation; p-values may be exact or approximate.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report Hodges–Lehmann pseudomedian shift and interval where appropriate, plus number of zero and nonzero differences.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect paired differences and symmetry; no model fit metric.
interpretation_guidance: Evidence of a positive signed-rank shift supports a systematically positive paired change.
common_misinterpretations: It is not simply a distribution-free paired t-test and is not always a test of the median difference without symmetry.
reporting_example: Wilcoxon signed-rank V = [V] (nonzero pairs = [n], p = [p]); estimated shift = [shift].

primary_outputs: Between-group F statistic, numerator and denominator degrees of freedom, group means and omnibus p-value.
inference_and_tests: Omnibus F test evaluates equality of all group means; specific pairwise claims require appropriate contrasts and multiplicity handling.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report group mean differences with intervals and η² or ω² with a clear denominator.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Examine model residuals and variance heterogeneity; R² or explained-variance fraction may be reported for equivalent linear models.
interpretation_guidance: A significant overall F suggests at least one group mean differs, not which pairs differ.
common_misinterpretations: An omnibus p-value is not proof that every group differs or that the group factor caused the differences.
reporting_example: One-way ANOVA: F([df1], [df2]) = [F], p = [p], ω² = [omega2]; contrasts were [method].

primary_outputs: F statistics for two factors and their interaction, degrees of freedom and estimated marginal means.
inference_and_tests: Separate tests assess each main effect and interaction; contrasts and multiplicity adjustments address detailed comparisons.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report interaction contrasts with confidence intervals; η² or partial η² with definition.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect model residuals, variance behavior and cell sizes; consider unbalanced-design sums-of-squares conventions.
interpretation_guidance: An interaction indicates the effect of one factor differs across levels of the other.
common_misinterpretations: Do not interpret an average main effect without considering a meaningful interaction or confuse association with causal effect.
reporting_example: Factor A × B interaction: F([df1], [df2]) = [F], p = [p], partial η² = [effect].

primary_outputs: Within-subject factor F statistic, degrees of freedom, estimated means and subject-level repeated changes.
inference_and_tests: Tests repeated-measure level effects; adjusted degrees of freedom (e.g., Greenhouse–Geisser) may be needed for >2 levels.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report pairwise within-person contrasts with intervals and generalized/partial η² with clear definition.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Examine repeated-measure covariance assumptions; sphericity is automatic with exactly two repeated levels.
interpretation_guidance: A significant time effect means at least one measurement occasion differs in average outcome.
common_misinterpretations: A time effect does not demonstrate treatment causality, and sphericity correction does not repair arbitrary missingness.
reporting_example: Repeated-measures ANOVA: F([df1], [df2]) = [F], p = [p] ([correction]); time contrast = [diff] [units].

primary_outputs: F tests for group, time and group × time interaction; cell means and estimated marginal means.
inference_and_tests: The interaction F test evaluates whether mean time profiles differ between groups, with degrees-of-freedom correction where applicable.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report the group × time contrast (e.g., difference in change) with a confidence interval and an appropriate ANOVA effect size.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect independence of groups, repeated-measure covariance and residuals; with two timepoints, sphericity needs no test.
interpretation_guidance: For two groups and two occasions, a positive difference-in-change means one group improved more on average than the other.
common_misinterpretations: A significant interaction is not automatically causal outside valid experimental or causal-identification assumptions.
reporting_example: Group × time: F([df1], [df2]) = [F], p = [p]; difference in change = [estimate] [units] (95% CI [lower], [upper]).

primary_outputs: Adjusted group means or contrast estimates, covariate coefficients, F/t statistics and p-values.
inference_and_tests: Tests adjusted group differences conditional on specified covariates; model-based inference depends on correct specification.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report adjusted mean difference and confidence interval; optionally partial η² for the group factor.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check linearity, residual structure, covariate overlap and homogeneity of slopes where assumed; model R² can supplement reporting.
interpretation_guidance: Adjusted differences compare groups at common model-defined covariate values.
common_misinterpretations: Adjustment alone does not remove unmeasured confounding; adjusting for a post-treatment variable can introduce bias.
reporting_example: Adjusted mean difference = [diff] [units] (95% CI [lower], [upper]); F([df1], [df2]) = [F], p = [p].

primary_outputs: Kruskal–Wallis H statistic, degrees of freedom, group rank summaries and p-value.
inference_and_tests: Omnibus rank test asks whether independent-group distributions differ; follow-up rank comparisons need multiplicity control.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report rank-based effect size (e.g., epsilon-squared) and an appropriate interval if supported.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Examine distribution shapes, ties and sample sizes; no model fit metric.
interpretation_guidance: An overall difference in ranks indicates groups are not distributed identically.
common_misinterpretations: Do not label the H test a general test of median differences unless comparable distribution shapes support that interpretation.
reporting_example: Kruskal–Wallis H([df]) = [H], p = [p], ε² = [effect]; post-hoc comparisons [method].

primary_outputs: Friedman chi-square statistic, degrees of freedom, block count and condition rank summaries.
inference_and_tests: Tests whether repeated-condition ranks are exchangeable across matched blocks; post-hoc comparisons require correction.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Kendall W describes concordance/effect magnitude on a bounded 0–1 scale; report uncertainty if available.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check complete matched blocks and valid within-block ranking; no general model fit index.
interpretation_guidance: Larger Kendall W reflects more consistently ordered conditions across blocks.
common_misinterpretations: This is not an analysis of arbitrary unbalanced longitudinal trajectories and does not identify which pairs differ by itself.
reporting_example: Friedman χ²([df]) = [stat], p = [p]; Kendall W = [W]; matched blocks = [n].

primary_outputs: Contingency table, Pearson chi-square statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value.
inference_and_tests: Tests statistical independence of categorical variables; expected-cell counts affect approximation quality.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report Cramér V (and, for 2×2 tables, risk/odds contrasts where scientifically relevant) with uncertainty if available.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check expected counts, missingness and independence; no prediction-model fit measure is inherent.
interpretation_guidance: Association means observed category combinations differ from independence expectations.
common_misinterpretations: A significant chi-square says nothing alone about effect size, direction, or causality.
reporting_example: χ²([df], N = [N]) = [stat], p = [p], Cramér V = [V].

primary_outputs: 2×2 or larger contingency table, Fisher exact p-value, and conditional odds ratio where applicable.
inference_and_tests: Exact conditional test evaluates independence for the chosen table, particularly useful with sparse counts.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: For a 2×2 table, report odds ratio and its exact/appropriate interval; describe the estimation method.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check table construction and independence of units; model fit indices do not apply.
interpretation_guidance: An odds ratio above 1 indicates higher odds in one category/group relative to the specified reference.
common_misinterpretations: An odds ratio is not a risk ratio, and an exact p-value does not eliminate selection bias or confounding.
reporting_example: Fisher exact p = [p]; odds ratio = [OR] (95% CI [lower], [upper]); table = [counts].

primary_outputs: Intercept and slope estimate, standard error, t statistic, fitted line and residuals.
inference_and_tests: Slope confidence interval and p-value test linear association under the regression error model.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report change in outcome units per one-unit change in predictor, with confidence interval and units.
fit_and_performance_metrics: R²/adjusted R² and residual summaries describe in-sample fit; out-of-sample RMSE assesses prediction when validated.
interpretation_guidance: A slope of 2 means expected Y rises by 2 units for each one-unit increase in X under the model.
common_misinterpretations: Association is not causation; a high R² does not guarantee unbiased coefficients or good extrapolation.
reporting_example: Linear slope β = [estimate] [Y units/X unit] (95% CI [lower], [upper]; p = [p]); R² = [R2].

primary_outputs: Regression coefficients, standard errors, model intercept and fitted predictions.
inference_and_tests: Conditional coefficient t tests and overall F test may be reported with intervals and multiplicity awareness.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report adjusted effect per predictor with confidence interval, specifying held-constant covariates.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Adjusted R², residual diagnostics and validated RMSE quantify different aspects of fit/performance.
interpretation_guidance: Each coefficient represents an expected change in Y per unit X when other included covariates are fixed.
common_misinterpretations: Statistical significance does not imply practical importance; collinearity or omitted variables can undermine interpretation.
reporting_example: Adjusted β[X] = [estimate] [units] (95% CI [lower], [upper]; p = [p]); adjusted R² = [R2adj].

primary_outputs: Log-odds coefficients, odds ratios (ORs), standard errors and predicted probabilities.
inference_and_tests: Wald or likelihood-ratio tests assess terms; confidence intervals can be obtained on log-odds or OR scale.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report adjusted OR with 95% CI and, where possible, meaningful absolute-risk differences or predicted probabilities.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Calibration, discrimination (AUC), log loss and validation address prediction; pseudo-R² is not ordinary variance explained.
interpretation_guidance: OR 1.5 corresponds to 50% higher odds, not necessarily 50% higher risk.
common_misinterpretations: Do not interpret ORs as risk ratios or infer performance from an in-sample classification cutoff alone.
reporting_example: Adjusted OR for [X] = [OR] (95% CI [lower], [upper]; p = [p]); validated AUC = [AUC] if predictive.

primary_outputs: Log-rate coefficients, incidence rate ratios (IRRs), predicted counts and exposure-offset specification.
inference_and_tests: Coefficient Wald/LR tests and confidence intervals apply under a specified count process.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: IRR with confidence interval describes multiplicative rates/count expectations conditional on model covariates and offset.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Assess overdispersion, excess zeros, residuals and predictive calibration; deviance/AIC are comparative, not absolute proof of fit.
interpretation_guidance: IRR 1.2 suggests an expected event rate 20% higher at the specified contrast.
common_misinterpretations: Ignoring unequal exposure times or substantial overdispersion can make results misleading; IRR is not a probability ratio.
reporting_example: IRR for [X] = [IRR] (95% CI [lower], [upper]); exposure offset = [unit]; dispersion check = [result].

primary_outputs: Fixed-effect coefficients, random-effect variance components, subject-specific fitted values and residual variance.
inference_and_tests: Conditional fixed-effect intervals/tests depend on degrees-of-freedom or likelihood procedure; report method used.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report key fixed contrasts with intervals and variance components; intraclass correlation can summarize clustering for relevant models.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Residual diagnostics and marginal/conditional R² or AIC (comparable likelihood fits) can inform model assessment.
interpretation_guidance: A fixed time-by-group coefficient estimates modeled average difference in change while random intercepts reflect subject heterogeneity.
common_misinterpretations: Do not treat random effects as independent participant observations or compare REML likelihoods across differing fixed-effect structures.
reporting_example: Fixed group × time β = [estimate] [units] (95% CI [lower], [upper]); random-intercept SD = [SD].

primary_outputs: Fixed-effect estimates on link scale, conditional predictions, random-effect variances and distribution family.
inference_and_tests: Wald/LR tests and intervals depend on family and approximation; report inferential method.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Exponentiated coefficients may be conditional ORs or IRRs for common logit/log-link families; include intervals.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Conditional/marginal predictions, residual checks and AIC for comparable likelihood fits; no universal R².
interpretation_guidance: In a logit GLMM an OR describes a conditional odds contrast given random effects, not a population-average contrast.
common_misinterpretations: Do not mix conditional GLMM effects with GEE population-average effects or interpret a GLMM OR as a risk ratio.
reporting_example: Conditional [OR/IRR] for [X] = [effect] (95% CI [lower], [upper]); random-effect variance = [var].

primary_outputs: Principal-component eigenvalues, component loadings/scores and proportion of total variance explained.
inference_and_tests: Ordinary PCA has no intrinsic coefficient p-values; resampling/permutation assesses component stability if required.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Explained-variance percentages and loadings show data compression, not causal effect size; uncertainty is not default.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Scree plot, reconstruction error and stability; no standard inferential model-fit p-value.
interpretation_guidance: A first component explaining 40% means it captures 40% of variation under the chosen scaling of included variables.
common_misinterpretations: High loadings do not establish a validated latent construct; PCA results depend on variable scaling.
reporting_example: PC1 explained [percent]% variance; highest absolute loadings were [variables] (scaling: [method]).

primary_outputs: Factor loadings, communalities, factor correlations and chosen factor count.
inference_and_tests: Exploratory factor extraction can include model-fit tests for some estimators; inference is conditional on extraction/rotation.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Loading magnitudes indicate association with common factors; bootstrap intervals may assess stability.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Parallel analysis, residual correlations, RMSEA/TLI for suitable common-factor fitting methods, and interpretability.
interpretation_guidance: A loading of 0.7 indicates a relatively strong modeled relationship between item and factor, not a 70% effect.
common_misinterpretations: An interpretable exploratory solution is not independent confirmation of construct validity.
reporting_example: [k]-factor EFA using [estimator/rotation] yielded salient loadings [range]; communalities [range]; fit [metric].

primary_outputs: Tree split rules, terminal-node predicted outcomes and variable-importance measures where available.
inference_and_tests: A standard prediction tree does not inherently test hypotheses with coefficient p-values.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Use predictive differences/probabilities and uncertainty from appropriate validation/resampling; importance is not a causal effect.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Report held-out RMSE/MAE for regression or AUC, calibration and confusion-matrix metrics for classification.
interpretation_guidance: A branch describes the model’s prediction for observations meeting a sequence of conditions.
common_misinterpretations: In-sample accuracy can be optimistic; split thresholds and importance are unstable and should not be treated as causal.
reporting_example: Held-out [metric] = [value]; tree depth = [depth]; key predictive splits = [variables].

primary_outputs: Ensemble predictions, out-of-bag or validation error, and optional variable-importance measures.
inference_and_tests: Classical coefficient p-values are not intrinsic; uncertainty can be studied with suitable resampling methods.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Compare calibrated predictions and meaningful outcome contrasts, with bootstrap or other suitable prediction intervals where justified.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Use out-of-bag or separate-test performance; report AUC/calibration for classification or RMSE/MAE for regression.
interpretation_guidance: Lower held-out prediction error indicates better generalization to similar unseen data under the validation design.
common_misinterpretations: Variable importance does not prove causality; out-of-bag evaluation may be insufficient under temporal or clustered dependence.
reporting_example: Random forest held-out [metric] = [value] ([resampling design]); predictors = [count].

primary_outputs: Treatment × post-period interaction estimate, standard error and group-period mean contrasts.
inference_and_tests: A confidence interval and p-value for the DiD interaction quantify statistical uncertainty, conditional on identification assumptions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: DiD estimate in outcome units is the treated-group change minus comparison-group change; report a confidence interval.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect pre-treatment trends, anticipation and composition; robust/clustered standard errors where warranted; R² is not causal validity.
interpretation_guidance: Estimate −3 means the treated group fell by three more outcome units than the comparison group over the period.
common_misinterpretations: Parallel trends cannot be established from a single baseline and post period; significance does not establish causal identification.
reporting_example: DiD = [estimate] [units] (95% CI [lower], [upper]; p = [p]); parallel-trends evidence = [assessment].

primary_outputs: Joint category counts and row, column or total percentages with clearly stated denominators.
inference_and_tests: Descriptive only; association tests such as chi-square or Fisher exact must be specified separately.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report differences in percentages, risk ratios or odds ratios with intervals when scientific comparisons warrant them.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check sparse cells, missing categories and denominators; model fit is not applicable.
interpretation_guidance: A row percentage answers what fraction of one row category is in a given column category.
common_misinterpretations: Row and column percentages answer different questions; a cross-tabulation alone does not establish statistical association.
reporting_example: Among [row category], [n]/[denominator] ([percent]%) had [column category].

primary_outputs: Point estimate, confidence level, confidence interval limits, and interval construction method.
inference_and_tests: Confidence intervals quantify long-run coverage of the interval procedure under its assumptions; an interval is not itself a hypothesis test.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Interval width reflects uncertainty about a specified estimand; choose a defensible method for means, proportions, differences or other targets.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check the estimator, dependence, weighting, sample size and method coverage; no model fit index is intrinsic.
interpretation_guidance: A 95% procedure would include the true fixed estimand in about 95% of repeated samples under its assumptions.
common_misinterpretations: Do not say a realized frequentist 95% interval gives a 95% probability that the fixed parameter lies inside it.
reporting_example: [Estimand] = [estimate] (95% CI [lower], [upper]; method = [interval method]).

primary_outputs: Kendall tau (tau-b when ties occur), sample size, concordant/discordant pair information.
inference_and_tests: Test for no rank association provides p-value with tie-aware approximation or exact calculation where appropriate.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Tau measures imbalance of concordance versus discordance; appropriate confidence intervals may be constructed.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect ordinal coding, ties and monotonic trend; no model fit statistic.
interpretation_guidance: Positive tau means concordant ordering of pairs is more common than discordant ordering.
common_misinterpretations: Tau is not a slope, an explained-variance percentage, or proof of causation.
reporting_example: Kendall τ-b = [tau] (95% CI [lower], [upper]; p = [p]; n = [n]).

primary_outputs: Point-biserial correlation r_pb, sample size and group-wise summary of continuous variable.
inference_and_tests: Equivalent standard inference to a two-group Pearson correlation/t test under the relevant assumptions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: r_pb summarizes standardized association between binary indicator and continuous variable; report CI and underlying group difference.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Examine group sizes, distribution and coding; no additional model fit metric.
interpretation_guidance: Positive r_pb means the category coded 1 has a higher average continuous outcome than category 0.
common_misinterpretations: Direction flips if binary coding is reversed; the correlation is not causal.
reporting_example: Point-biserial r = [r] (95% CI [lower], [upper], n = [n]); binary coding: [0/1 labels].

primary_outputs: Partial correlation r between two variables conditional on specified covariates.
inference_and_tests: Tests and confidence intervals are conditional on adjustment set and model assumptions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report partial r and confidence interval alongside the exact covariate set.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Examine linearity, residual dependence, covariate quality and sensitivity to adjustment; no universal goodness-of-fit statistic.
interpretation_guidance: Partial r measures remaining linear association after removing modeled associations with selected covariates.
common_misinterpretations: Partialling out covariates does not automatically identify a causal relationship; adjusting for colliders can create bias.
reporting_example: Partial r(X,Y | [covariates]) = [r] (95% CI [lower], [upper], p = [p]).

primary_outputs: Sample mean, reference value, one-sample t statistic and degrees of freedom.
inference_and_tests: Tests whether a population mean equals a prespecified reference value.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Mean difference from reference and 95% confidence interval; optionally standardized effect d with its definition.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect observations, outliers and sample-distribution concerns; no model fit index.
interpretation_guidance: A difference of +5 indicates the sample mean is five measurement units above the prespecified reference.
common_misinterpretations: Failure to reject does not establish equivalence, and data-driven reference choices invalidate ordinary p-value interpretation.
reporting_example: Mean − reference = [diff] [units] (95% CI [lower], [upper]); t([df]) = [t], p = [p].

primary_outputs: Welch heteroscedastic omnibus F statistic, approximate degrees of freedom and group summaries.
inference_and_tests: Tests equality of independent-group means allowing unequal variances; use suitable unequal-variance post-hoc contrasts.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report group mean differences with heteroscedastic confidence intervals and appropriate standardized effect when useful.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect independence, small cell sizes and outliers; no stand-alone predictive fit measure.
interpretation_guidance: A significant Welch F implies at least one mean is different, without specifying which.
common_misinterpretations: Welch ANOVA does not fix non-independence or identify specific group differences without contrasts.
reporting_example: Welch F([df1], [df2]) = [F], p = [p]; unequal-variance post-hoc method = [method].

primary_outputs: Multivariate test statistics (e.g., Pillai trace), approximate F and degrees of freedom, outcomes and group contrasts.
inference_and_tests: Overall MANOVA tests whether the multivariate mean vector differs; follow-up tests require multiplicity and correlation awareness.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report multivariate effect index alongside each outcome’s estimated mean contrast with interval.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect multivariate residual structure, group covariance and influential observations; report chosen multivariate statistic.
interpretation_guidance: Significant Pillai trace suggests the groups differ somewhere in the joint set of continuous outcomes.
common_misinterpretations: An omnibus result does not establish that every outcome differs; univariate tests alone discard multivariate context.
reporting_example: MANOVA Pillai trace = [V], F([df1], [df2]) = [F], p = [p]; outcomes = [list].

primary_outputs: 2×2 paired binary table, discordant-pair counts and McNemar test statistic/p-value.
inference_and_tests: Tests equality of two marginal binary proportions under paired observations; exact variant can be used for few discordant pairs.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report paired proportion difference with suitable interval and/or matched-pair odds ratio with its definition.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect pairing, discordant counts and sampling; no predictive model-fit statistic.
interpretation_guidance: More changes from no→yes than yes→no indicates a net shift in positive responses.
common_misinterpretations: McNemar does not analyze two independent groups; concordant pairs do not drive the basic test statistic.
reporting_example: Discordant pairs: no→yes = [b], yes→no = [c]; McNemar p = [p]; paired difference = [diff].

primary_outputs: Linear and polynomial-term coefficients, fitted curves and predicted means.
inference_and_tests: Individual term tests and joint polynomial comparisons may assess curvature, but depend on model specification.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report predicted outcome contrasts or marginal slopes at meaningful predictor values with intervals.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Adjusted R², residual plots, and cross-validated prediction error; compare polynomials at same dataset/design.
interpretation_guidance: A significant quadratic term suggests modeled curvature, but the practical pattern is best shown with fitted predictions.
common_misinterpretations: A polynomial coefficient alone is not a constant change per X unit, and high-degree fits can extrapolate wildly.
reporting_example: Quadratic term β₂ = [value] (p = [p]); predicted Y at X = [x1] versus [x2] differed by [diff] (95% CI [limits]).

primary_outputs: Smooth-function estimates and plots, effective degrees of freedom (EDF), fitted values and uncertainty bands.
inference_and_tests: Approximate smooth-term tests/p-values depend on smoothing selection and model family; avoid overinterpreting exploratory smooths.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report meaningful predicted contrasts or derivative estimates with uncertainty bands, not only a smooth-term p-value.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Deviance explained, adjusted R² where meaningful, residual diagnostics and held-out predictive error.
interpretation_guidance: EDF above one can indicate nonlinear complexity, while the smooth plot shows its estimated shape.
common_misinterpretations: EDF is not a conventional coefficient or effect size; smoothing bands are not evidence of causality.
reporting_example: Smooth of [X]: EDF = [edf], approximate p = [p]; predicted outcome difference [x1]→[x2] = [diff].

primary_outputs: Category-specific log-odds coefficients and predicted probabilities relative to a chosen outcome reference category.
inference_and_tests: Wald or likelihood-ratio tests and confidence intervals apply to coefficients or whole predictors.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report relative risk ratios (exponentiated multinomial logit coefficients) with intervals and/or category probability contrasts.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Validate multiclass log loss, calibration and discrimination; pseudo-R² does not equal ordinary variance explained.
interpretation_guidance: A relative risk ratio above 1 favors one outcome category over the reference category as X increases.
common_misinterpretations: Relative risk ratio in multinomial logit is not an epidemiologic risk ratio; results depend on outcome reference category.
reporting_example: For category [k] vs [reference], RRR([X]) = [RRR] (95% CI [limits]); predicted P(category [k]) = [p].

primary_outputs: Cumulative log-odds coefficient(s), threshold parameters and predicted ordinal-category probabilities.
inference_and_tests: Coefficient Wald/LR tests and confidence intervals depend on link and proportional-odds specification.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report common odds ratio with interval if proportional-odds model holds, or category-specific contrasts if it does not.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check proportional-odds assumption and ordinal calibration; use appropriate predictive scoring metrics.
interpretation_guidance: OR above 1 shifts cumulative-category odds according to the software’s stated coding convention.
common_misinterpretations: The direction of an ordinal OR depends on response ordering and link convention; never assume every OR means higher severity.
reporting_example: Ordinal OR for [X] = [OR] (95% CI [limits]); outcome ordering = [levels]; proportional odds check = [result].

primary_outputs: Log-mean coefficients, IRRs, dispersion parameter and predicted event counts.
inference_and_tests: Wald/LR tests and intervals quantify term uncertainty under a specified negative-binomial parameterization.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: IRR and interval describe expected multiplicative count/rate changes; specify any exposure offset.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check dispersion, residuals and zero frequencies; AIC/deviance can compare suitable count models.
interpretation_guidance: IRR 0.8 indicates 20% lower expected event rate for the named contrast with other covariates held fixed.
common_misinterpretations: Negative binomial is not automatically needed for every count outcome; dispersion parameter meanings differ among implementations.
reporting_example: Negative-binomial IRR([X]) = [IRR] (95% CI [limits]); dispersion = [parameter]; offset = [exposure].

primary_outputs: Separate count-model and zero-inflation component estimates, predicted zero probability and conditional count mean.
inference_and_tests: Wald/LR tests can examine model terms; tests at boundaries or comparing non-nested models require suitable methodology.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report component-specific coefficients/IRRs or ORs with intervals and marginal predicted count contrasts.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Compare observed and predicted zero frequencies, calibration and suitable information criteria/validated log scores.
interpretation_guidance: A predictor can affect the structural-zero component differently from the count-generating component.
common_misinterpretations: Do not treat count-component IRR as the marginal overall mean ratio or assume observed zeros prove a separate zero-generating process.
reporting_example: Count-component IRR([X]) = [value]; zero-component OR([X]) = [value]; fitted P(Y=0) = [value].

primary_outputs: Link-scale coefficients, fitted mean proportions and optional precision/dispersion parameter.
inference_and_tests: Term tests and confidence intervals are model-dependent and often reported on link or response scale.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report predicted mean-proportion contrasts with intervals; exponentiated logit-link coefficients describe odds of the mean proportion.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect fitted proportions, residuals, boundary values and model comparison criteria where suitable.
interpretation_guidance: A modeled rise from 0.30 to 0.35 is a five-percentage-point change in expected proportion.
common_misinterpretations: Standard beta regression excludes exact zero and one unless extended; coefficients are not raw proportion-point effects.
reporting_example: Predicted mean proportion at X = [x1] was [p1] versus [p2] at [x2] (difference [delta], 95% CI [limits]).

primary_outputs: Conditional quantile-regression coefficients for prespecified quantile τ and predicted conditional quantiles.
inference_and_tests: Use suitable rank, asymptotic or bootstrap intervals/tests accounting for the sample design.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report quantile-specific slope or predicted quantile difference with confidence interval and units.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check quantile crossing, residual patterns and out-of-sample pinball loss; R² from least squares is not the primary fit measure.
interpretation_guidance: At τ = 0.90, a slope of 2 estimates a two-unit difference in the conditional 90th percentile per X unit.
common_misinterpretations: A conditional quantile slope does not necessarily describe changes for individuals who stay at the same percentile.
reporting_example: At τ = [tau], quantile slope for [X] = [estimate] [units] (95% CI [limits]).

primary_outputs: Population-average regression coefficients, working-correlation estimates and robust/sandwich standard errors.
inference_and_tests: Wald tests and confidence intervals are commonly based on cluster-robust variance; small-cluster corrections may be needed.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report marginal effect as mean difference, OR or IRR according to chosen link, with cluster-aware interval.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Assess cluster counts, marginal mean specification and residuals; QIC may compare GEE models, not ordinary AIC by default.
interpretation_guidance: A GEE logit OR summarizes a population-average odds contrast, different from a subject-specific mixed-model OR.
common_misinterpretations: Working correlation need not be exactly correct for robust large-cluster inference, but few clusters can invalidate simple SEs.
reporting_example: GEE population-average [effect] = [estimate] (95% robust CI [limits]); clusters = [n].

primary_outputs: Log-hazard coefficients, hazard ratios (HRs), standard errors and adjusted survival predictions.
inference_and_tests: Wald, score or LR tests and confidence intervals describe relative hazards under proportional-hazards and censoring assumptions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: HR with CI is a relative instantaneous hazard contrast, not a risk ratio or absolute survival difference.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Schoenfeld residuals address proportional-hazards; concordance and calibration assess predictive aspects; likelihood metrics compare fits.
interpretation_guidance: HR = 1.4 indicates an estimated 40% greater instantaneous hazard at a given time conditional on the model.
common_misinterpretations: HR 1.4 does not mean 40% more people experience the event or a 40% shorter survival time.
reporting_example: Adjusted HR([X]) = [HR] (95% CI [limits]; p = [p]); proportional-hazards assessment = [result].

primary_outputs: Kaplan–Meier survival estimates S(t), numbers at risk, censor counts and median survival when estimable.
inference_and_tests: Pointwise survival confidence intervals can be shown; group comparisons require a separate procedure such as log-rank test.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report survival probability at prespecified times with CI and median survival with CI when estimable.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Show numbers at risk and censoring pattern; an in-sample global model-fit statistic is not intrinsic.
interpretation_guidance: S(12 months)=0.8 estimates the fraction remaining event-free at 12 months under censoring assumptions.
common_misinterpretations: A Kaplan–Meier curve is not a causal treatment comparison; median survival may be not reached.
reporting_example: At [time], estimated survival was [S] (95% CI [limits]); at risk = [n].

primary_outputs: Log-rank chi-square statistic, degrees of freedom, group survival curves and p-value.
inference_and_tests: Tests the null of equal event-time distributions under the risk-set weighting used; interpretation depends on independent censoring.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report survival differences at meaningful times and CIs separately; a log-rank test alone has no HR estimate.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect Kaplan–Meier curves, crossings and at-risk numbers; model-fit statistics are not part of the test.
interpretation_guidance: A significant test indicates evidence of differing event-time experiences between groups.
common_misinterpretations: A non-significant log-rank test does not prove equal survival and may miss important crossing hazards.
reporting_example: Log-rank χ²([df]) = [stat], p = [p]; survival at [time] differed by [diff] percentage points.

primary_outputs: Standardized factor loadings, latent-factor correlations, standard errors and model fit indices.
inference_and_tests: Model chi-square tests exact-fit null; loading tests and CIs depend on estimator and identification.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report loadings and confidence intervals, factor correlations and meaningful reliability evidence.
fit_and_performance_metrics: CFI/TLI, RMSEA with CI and SRMR summarize different misfit aspects; threshold cutoffs are context-dependent.
interpretation_guidance: A high loading indicates an indicator tracks its modeled latent factor after accounting for its scale.
common_misinterpretations: Good global fit alone does not prove construct validity or population measurement invariance.
reporting_example: CFA: χ²([df]) = [stat], CFI = [CFI], TLI = [TLI], RMSEA = [RMSEA] (90% CI [limits]), SRMR = [SRMR].

primary_outputs: Estimated standardized/unstandardized path coefficients, variances and, where overidentified, global model fit.
inference_and_tests: Path coefficients have model-based standard errors, intervals and tests; indirect effects may need resampling.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report direct/indirect path estimates with confidence intervals, specifying scale and adjustment.
fit_and_performance_metrics: χ², CFI/TLI, RMSEA and SRMR are meaningful for identified overidentified models; saturated models do not test global fit.
interpretation_guidance: A path coefficient quantifies a modeled conditional association along the specified directed edge.
common_misinterpretations: Arrows do not create causal identification; an excellent fit does not prove the proposed direction of causation.
reporting_example: Path X→Y = [beta] (95% CI [limits]); global fit = [indices or saturated model].

primary_outputs: Measurement loadings, structural coefficients, latent covariances and model fit indices.
inference_and_tests: Parameter intervals/tests depend on estimator and identification; model chi-square addresses exact covariance structure under assumptions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report standardized and unstandardized effects, intervals, and indirect effects where appropriate.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Use χ², degrees of freedom, CFI/TLI, RMSEA with interval and SRMR; assess local fit and alternative plausible models.
interpretation_guidance: A structural path quantifies the modeled relationship between latent/observed variables given the specified measurement structure.
common_misinterpretations: Fit indices are not probabilities the theory is true; the same covariance structure may be produced by competing models.
reporting_example: SEM: χ²([df]) = [stat], CFI = [CFI], RMSEA = [RMSEA], SRMR = [SRMR]; path β = [beta] (CI [limits]).

primary_outputs: Total, direct and indirect effect estimates, mediator path estimates and their uncertainty.
inference_and_tests: Bootstrap or appropriate analytical intervals test indirect effects under the model and identification assumptions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report indirect effect a×b and confidence interval; proportion mediated is often unstable and needs careful definition.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Inspect sensitivity to mediator–outcome confounding and functional form; global fit indices depend on mediation model chosen.
interpretation_guidance: An indirect-effect estimate describes a modeled pathway contribution under strong causal assumptions when interpreted causally.
common_misinterpretations: Statistical mediation alone does not demonstrate a causal mechanism, even in a randomized treatment trial.
reporting_example: Indirect effect = [estimate] (95% bootstrap CI [limits]); direct effect = [estimate]; assumptions = [summary].

primary_outputs: Estimated latent intercept/slope means, factor variances/covariances and trajectory-class predictors where specified.
inference_and_tests: Tests and intervals quantify growth-factor parameters under trajectory and missing-data assumptions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report mean rate of change with CI, between-person variance in slopes and key model contrasts.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Compare identified models with CFI/TLI, RMSEA/SRMR where applicable and likelihood criteria for comparable fits.
interpretation_guidance: Positive mean latent slope means the population trajectory generally increases per chosen time unit.
common_misinterpretations: Assuming linear growth when trajectories curve can mislead; model fit does not establish causal influences on growth.
reporting_example: Mean latent slope = [estimate] [units/time] (95% CI [limits]); slope variance = [var]; CFI = [value].

primary_outputs: Estimated ARIMA orders (p,d,q), coefficients, residuals and forecasts with prediction intervals.
inference_and_tests: Coefficient intervals may be available; forecast evaluation is more useful than treating individual term p-values as primary conclusions.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report forecast point estimates and interval bands, horizon and uncertainty assumptions.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Evaluate rolling-origin RMSE/MAE/MASE and residual autocorrelation (e.g., Ljung–Box); use AICc for suitable candidate order comparisons.
interpretation_guidance: Forecast intervals widen when uncertainty accumulates across longer horizons under the assumed stochastic model.
common_misinterpretations: A low in-sample AIC does not guarantee future forecasting accuracy, especially across structural breaks.
reporting_example: ARIMA([p],[d],[q]) produced [h]-step forecast [value] (95% PI [lower], [upper]); rolling MAE = [MAE].

primary_outputs: Estimated level/trend/seasonal state parameters, forecasts and prediction intervals.
inference_and_tests: ETS is primarily a forecasting framework; component significance tests are not generally the focus.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report point forecasts and prediction intervals, with horizon and outcome units.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Compare rolling-origin MAE/RMSE/MASE, residual whiteness and AICc among suitable ETS structures.
interpretation_guidance: The modeled level, trend and seasonality extrapolate historical patterns subject to forecast uncertainty.
common_misinterpretations: Good training fit does not ensure future performance after an intervention or structural shift.
reporting_example: ETS([error],[trend],[season]) forecast at [h] = [value] (95% PI [limits]); validation MASE = [value].

primary_outputs: Baseline level/trend, immediate level-change coefficient and post-intervention slope-change coefficient.
inference_and_tests: Intervals and tests on level and slope changes require correct serial-correlation handling and prespecified intervention timing.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report level shift and trend change with intervals; forecast counterfactual differences at meaningful times where justified.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Check pre-intervention trend, seasonality, autocorrelation, concurrent events and model residuals; AIC is not a causal validity check.
interpretation_guidance: A negative level-change estimate represents an immediate modeled drop at interruption; slope change describes subsequent divergence.
common_misinterpretations: Changes may reflect concurrent events; one or two pre-periods are insufficient for credible trend modeling.
reporting_example: Immediate level change = [estimate] (95% CI [limits]); slope change = [estimate] per period; serial correlation handled by [method].

primary_outputs: Propensity scores, matching/weighting diagnostics, covariate balance, treatment-effect estimate.
inference_and_tests: Inference for ATT/ATE depends on estimator, overlap, weighting/matching uncertainty and outcome model.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report target estimand (ATE or ATT), effect in outcome units or risk scale, and CI using appropriate robust/resampling variance.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Standardized mean differences, weight distributions, effective sample size and overlap are central; propensity model AUC alone is not enough.
interpretation_guidance: After acceptable covariate balance, the estimated contrast compares treatment groups on the chosen estimand scale.
common_misinterpretations: Observed covariate balance cannot rule out unmeasured confounding; propensity score quality is not judged by classification accuracy.
reporting_example: [ATE/ATT] = [estimate] [units] (95% CI [limits]); max absolute standardized difference after adjustment = [value].

primary_outputs: Boosted predictions, tuned learning rate/iterations and optional feature contribution summaries.
inference_and_tests: Predictive model has no inherent coefficient p-values; use resampling for uncertainty where meaningful.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report predicted-risk or predicted-outcome contrast and calibrated probability/intervals if available, not causal feature importance.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Use held-out log loss/AUC/calibration for classification or RMSE/MAE for regression, with leakage-free validation.
interpretation_guidance: Better independent-test scoring means more accurate predictions in the evaluated population, not better causal explanation.
common_misinterpretations: Feature importance or SHAP contribution is model-specific and not an experimental effect.
reporting_example: Gradient boosting held-out [metric] = [value] under [validation design]; calibration [metric] = [value].

primary_outputs: Shrinkage coefficients, selected penalty strength λ and predicted outcomes.
inference_and_tests: Standard OLS coefficient p-values/CIs do not generally apply after ridge penalization; specialized inference is needed.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report prediction changes or coefficient patterns and validated predictive uncertainty where appropriate.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Cross-validated RMSE/MAE or deviance and selected λ are central; no simple post-penalization ordinary R² inference.
interpretation_guidance: Ridge shrinks correlated predictor coefficients toward zero while retaining them in a typical linear implementation.
common_misinterpretations: Coefficient magnitudes depend on scaling and penalty; shrinkage is not variable selection or proof of mechanism.
reporting_example: Ridge λ = [lambda] by [CV scheme]; held-out RMSE = [RMSE]; predictors standardized [yes/no].

primary_outputs: LASSO coefficients, nonzero selected predictors, chosen λ and validation predictions.
inference_and_tests: Naive post-selection p-values/CIs are not valid without methods addressing selection.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report coefficient selection stability and predictive contrasts, not uncorrected inferential claims.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Cross-validated RMSE/deviance or holdout metrics; selected λ and nonzero coefficient count.
interpretation_guidance: A coefficient shrunk to zero means this penalty setting excluded its contribution, not that the true effect is exactly zero.
common_misinterpretations: Selection can change with small data perturbations, especially for correlated predictors; scaling strongly matters.
reporting_example: LASSO at λ = [lambda] retained [k] predictors; validation [metric] = [value].

primary_outputs: Elastic-net coefficients, penalty magnitude λ, mixing parameter α and predictions.
inference_and_tests: Ordinary unpenalized coefficient tests are not valid after selection/shrinkage without specialized inference.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report selected coefficient patterns, stability and validated predictive performance.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Use nested/appropriate cross-validation to tune α and λ; report held-out loss or calibration.
interpretation_guidance: Elastic net combines L1 and L2 shrinkage and can retain groups of correlated predictors in some settings.
common_misinterpretations: A selected predictor is not necessarily a causal driver; coefficient scale depends on standardization and tuning.
reporting_example: Elastic net α = [alpha], λ = [lambda]; [k] nonzero terms; held-out [metric] = [value].

primary_outputs: Decision scores or predicted labels; support-vector counts, kernel and hyperparameters.
inference_and_tests: Standard SVM is not a hypothesis-testing procedure; probability estimates require calibration.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report margins or calibrated probabilities and corresponding uncertainty from appropriate validation where possible.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Use held-out accuracy/F1/AUC and class-specific sensitivity, specificity or regression RMSE; tune within validation.
interpretation_guidance: A larger decision score generally indicates the prediction lies further toward one class side of the separating boundary.
common_misinterpretations: SVM decision scores are not automatically probabilities, and accuracy alone can mislead with class imbalance.
reporting_example: SVM [kernel], tuned C = [value]; held-out sensitivity = [value], specificity = [value], AUC = [value].

primary_outputs: Nearest-neighbor class votes or averaged predicted outcomes, distance metric and chosen k.
inference_and_tests: kNN has no default coefficient p-values; quantify predictive uncertainty through separate validation/resampling.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report predicted class probability from neighbor votes only with calibration checks; regression effects are local prediction differences.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Held-out accuracy/AUC/log loss or RMSE/MAE, with tuning k and preprocessing performed within validation folds.
interpretation_guidance: A classification is determined by the classes of nearby training observations under the chosen distance.
common_misinterpretations: Predictions depend heavily on scaling, distance, class balance and leakage; kNN neighborhood proportion is not automatically calibrated.
reporting_example: kNN k = [k], distance = [metric]; held-out [metric] = [value]; features scaled [method].

primary_outputs: Predicted class probabilities, estimated class priors and conditional feature likelihoods.
inference_and_tests: No inherent coefficient-significance tests; validation quantifies predictive utility and probability calibration.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Compare calibrated predicted risks and classification metrics, not causal variable-effect estimates.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Held-out log loss, Brier score, calibration and AUC/accuracy; inspect sensitivity to violated conditional independence.
interpretation_guidance: The algorithm combines class priors and feature evidence under conditional-independence assumptions.
common_misinterpretations: Strong classification accuracy does not imply the feature-independence assumption holds or estimated probabilities are calibrated.
reporting_example: Naive Bayes held-out AUC = [AUC], log loss = [loss], and calibration assessment = [result].

primary_outputs: Predicted classes/probabilities or continuous outcomes, fitted network specification and training history.
inference_and_tests: Neural networks lack default classical coefficient p-values; uncertainty requires deliberate calibration or resampling.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report meaningful predicted contrasts and prediction intervals or calibrated probabilities when available.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Held-out loss, calibration, AUC or RMSE; examine training/validation gap and robustness to initialization.
interpretation_guidance: A model can accurately capture complex patterns without yielding a transparent statistical effect for any one feature.
common_misinterpretations: Attribution scores are model-explanation tools, not proof of causal importance; large training accuracy can reflect overfitting.
reporting_example: Network [architecture] achieved held-out [metric] = [value] under [validation scheme].

primary_outputs: Cluster assignments, centroids, within-cluster sum of squares and selected k.
inference_and_tests: Ordinary k-means has no automatic p-values or confidence intervals for clusters.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report cluster sizes, centroid differences and stability rather than causal effect sizes.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Within-cluster sum of squares, silhouette score and stability are descriptive selection criteria; no universal fit threshold.
interpretation_guidance: Clusters group observations relatively close under the specified scaled distance and chosen k.
common_misinterpretations: Cluster membership is not evidence of true natural subpopulations; changing scaling or k can substantially alter results.
reporting_example: k-means k = [k]; cluster sizes = [sizes]; mean silhouette = [score]; stability = [assessment].

primary_outputs: Dendrogram, linkage heights, cluster assignments after tree cut and cluster profiles.
inference_and_tests: Standard hierarchical clustering has no automatic p-values or confidence intervals for branches.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Summarize separation, cluster stability and descriptive differences, not treatment effects.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Cophenetic correlation and cluster stability may characterize hierarchy; silhouette may help choose cut level.
interpretation_guidance: Merge heights describe dissimilarity under the chosen distance/linkage, not significance of a biological division.
common_misinterpretations: Branches can shift with scaling and linkage choice; a dendrogram does not validate the number of real clusters.
reporting_example: Hierarchical clustering used [distance] and [linkage]; cut at k = [k], silhouette = [value].

primary_outputs: Core, border and noise labels, cluster sizes and hyperparameters epsilon/minPts.
inference_and_tests: DBSCAN is unsupervised and does not inherently produce significance tests or parameter intervals.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report cluster composition, noise fraction and stability under reasonable parameter perturbations.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Density-cluster stability and domain usefulness matter; silhouette is sometimes misleading for non-convex or noise-rich clusters.
interpretation_guidance: Noise points were not assigned to a sufficiently dense region under the selected distance and parameters.
common_misinterpretations: A noise label does not prove an observation is an error or anomaly; results depend on density scale and metric.
reporting_example: DBSCAN ε = [epsilon], minPts = [n]; clusters = [k], noise fraction = [percent]%; stability = [result].

primary_outputs: Anomaly scores, flagged records and contamination/threshold choice.
inference_and_tests: Isolation Forest does not intrinsically yield p-values for anomalous observations.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report proportions flagged, score distributions and precision/recall against independently labeled anomalies if available.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Evaluate stability and external validation; false-positive rate depends on labeling and threshold.
interpretation_guidance: An unusually high anomaly score means a case is isolated quickly relative to the fitted reference distribution.
common_misinterpretations: A flagged observation is not necessarily erroneous, fraudulent or clinically abnormal.
reporting_example: Isolation Forest flagged [n] of [N] records ([percent]%) at threshold [rule]; validated precision = [value] if known.

primary_outputs: Exposure–response–lag surface, individual-lag and cumulative association estimates, model predictions.
inference_and_tests: Pointwise and cumulative confidence intervals/tests depend on basis specification and time-series dependence handling.
effect_sizes_and_intervals: Report relative risk or outcome difference at specified exposures and lags, with cumulative effect and 95% CI.
fit_and_performance_metrics: Assess basis choice, maximum lag, residual autocorrelation and robustness to temporal confounding; AIC only compares specified models.
interpretation_guidance: A cumulative relative risk of 1.2 at a specified exposure compares modeled accumulated risk over the defined lag window with a reference exposure.
common_misinterpretations: Do not interpret multiple lag-specific peaks as independent effects or assume observed exposure–lag associations are causal.
reporting_example: For [exposure] versus [reference] over lags 0–[L], cumulative [RR/difference] = [estimate] (95% CI [limits]).
